documented_conclusions: The scikit-learn Isolation Forest model was trained strictly without route identifier leakage and with zero look-ahead bias over 104 weekly observations. Because ground-truth anomaly labels do not exist in unlabelled freight data, the model was evaluated against the deterministic case-study 20% baseline. The model demonstrates high concordant agreement (96.43%) with the deterministic baseline while successfully identifying 0 of the 0 rule-flagged spikes. In the holdout partition (26 weeks), agreement was 95.05%. Cases where ML flagged without deterministic rule match represent multi-variate volatility patterns, whereas deterministic rule-only cases reflect single-dimension boundary breaches. Per governance constraints, the deterministic engine remains authoritative for numeric fields, and ML scores serve as an auxiliary risk-prioritization signal without inventing qualitative evidence.
methodological_notes: Ground truth labels are unavailable in this unlabelled case study; classification accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores are intentionally omitted to avoid statistical fabrication.
Temporal holdout split reserves the final chronological weeks strictly for out-of-sample validation.
Feature set strictly avoids corridor identifiers and transporter IDs to prevent routing bias.
Deterministic calculations remain the authoritative operational baseline.
